solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Problem creating rheumatism makes mother quiet

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, played quietly

explanation.surface: A mother keeps silent about the ailment causing her aching joints.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet conditions are blamed for aching joints, so moisture is a problem that brings on rheumatic pain.

clue.text: Objects seen as odd turning up in possession of some Parisian

indicators.note: being held in someone's possession means sitting inside them, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: des is the French word for 'some', as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means the word for odd is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: rum means strange or odd

explanation.surface: Someone notices peculiar items belonging to a Parisian surfacing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some Parisian' asks for French: the partitive article meaning 'some'. 'turning up' makes MUR, which sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To object is to raise a protest, which is what someone who demurs does; both are verbs in the third person.

clue.text: Silly person runs into a huge mass of rock!

indicators.note: one piece going into another signals that it is placed inside it

parts.note: the moon is a vast body of rock orbiting Earth
r is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A fool charges headlong into an enormous boulder, the exclamation mark relishing the slapstick.
explanation.definitionFit: A dimwit is a foolish person, an insulting synonym for someone lacking sense.

clue.text: Place of miracle attended by sick Eastern people en masse

parts.note: Cana in Galilee is where Jesus turned water into wine
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Crowds of sick people from the East flock to a site of miraculous healing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attended by' simply places the pieces one after another.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a scornful term for the rabble, the common people considered as a mob.

clue.text: Group in bed overlooking lake

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece overlooking another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A party of people lies in bed in a room with a view over a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A clique, an exclusive circle of people sharing an interest, is a kind of group.

clue.text: Old phone used in final brief communication

indicators.note: being used in something means being put inside it

parts.note: net means final, as in a net result after deductions
tel is the abbreviation for telephone

explanation.surface: An antique telephone carries the last short message.
explanation.definitionFit: A short letter or note written on a small folded sheet is a brief written communication.

clue.text: Seduce American naughtily offering sweet food

indicators.note: behaving naughtily means misbehaving, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A wicked plan to win over a Yank by plying them with dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: This dessert of frozen confection topped with syrup and nuts is a sweet treat.

clue.text: Philosopher needing money to acquire new suit

parts.note: lucre is money, often ill-gotten

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of suit are made anew in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A thinker needs cash to buy a fresh outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' makes TIUS from the outfit word; 'needing' and 'to acquire' just join the pieces. The Roman philosopher is less familiar than the money word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman poet who wrote De Rerum Natura expounded Epicurean thought, so he counts as a philosopher.

clue.text: I'm a beach thing constructed to hide person's bottom maybe

definitions.text: I'm a beach thing constructed to hide person's bottom maybe

indicators.note: hiding something means keeping it within, so one piece is placed inside the other
something constructed is assembled, so the letters of the phrase are put together in a new order
the bottom of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A seaside contraption speaks, boasting it was built to keep a bather's backside from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constructed' rearranges I'M A BEACH THING, and 'to hide' places N, the bottom of 'person's', inside. The whole clue also describes the thing: 'maybe' admits the hidden bottom is only a playful example.
explanation.definitionFit: Victorian wheeled huts were rolled into the sea so bathers could change and enter the water unseen, preserving modesty.

clue.text: Time boys gets immersed under water

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece under another comes after it

parts.note: the sea is a body of water
a son is a boy; the plural is loose, as one boy is all that is needed

explanation.surface: Lads take a dip and are submerged beneath the waves for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets immersed under' places the boy below the sea in the grid; only one son is needed despite the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: A season is a period of the year, such as summer, so it is a stretch of time.

clue.text: Bitter matron wandering round end of ward

indicators.note: going round something means enclosing it
wandering means straying about, so the letters of matron move into a new order
the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: A sour hospital matron strolls about the far end of the ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' turns MATRON into MORANT, and 'round' puts it around D, the end of 'ward'.
explanation.definitionFit: Biting, caustic wit is called sharp or cutting, so bitter remarks fit this adjective.

clue.text: Sentimentality of elder maybe, enthralling a class

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: the elder is an example of a tree
cl is the abbreviation for class

explanation.surface: An older person's mushy feelings captivate a class of pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elder maybe' is a tree, not an older person; 'maybe' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloying syrup gives a figurative sense of sickly sweetness in speech or feeling, i.e. mawkish emotion.

clue.text: Farmer rushed around pursued by that woman

indicators.note: being pursued by means having something follow behind, so that piece comes after

parts.note: ran means rushed
c, short for circa, means around or approximately
her refers to a woman already mentioned

explanation.surface: A farmer hurried about, chased by a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who owns or runs a large livestock farm, especially in America, is a kind of farmer.

clue.text: Gift from girl full of passion, article not acceptable

indicators.note: being full of something means containing it

parts.note: a lass is a girl

indicators.note: something not acceptable is excluded, so the article is dropped

parts.note: rage is a passion or fury
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A present from a passionate girl turns out to be an unacceptable item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not acceptable' leaves RGE; 'article' here is grammatical, not a thing given. This older spelling ends in a double S rather than -ESSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous giving of money or presents, especially by the powerful, means a bountiful gift.

clue.text: Single-mindedness of canon, contrite after going astray

indicators.note: going astray means wandering off course, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A cathedral clergyman, sorry after sinning, shows a resolute focus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canon' looks like the cleric of the surface, but it is merely letters, as is the penitent word; 'after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Close mental focus on one task is single-minded attention.

clue.text: Successive actions by batsman to get out of trouble quickly

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a cut is a stroke played square, after which the batsman can take a run

definitions.text: to get out of trouble quickly
definitions.meaning: to make a hasty escape, leaving a situation behind

explanation.surface: A batsman plays his shots in quick succession to escape a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a cut is a shot played to the off side; a batsman then sets off for a run.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means fleeing quickly from difficulty, and literally names a cricket stroke followed by a sprint between wickets.

clue.text: Splashing shampoo, mister effects a complete transformation

indicators.note: splashing scatters things around, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A gentleman sloshing hair wash about undergoes a total makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: The change of a caterpillar into a butterfly is the model of a total change of form.

clue.text: Apes in Civil Service led by somewhat cold female

indicators.note: being led by means having something go in front, so that piece comes first

parts.note: Mimi is the heroine of Puccini's La Boheme, whose tiny hand is frozen

explanation.surface: Primates in government service are under a chilly woman's leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: Mimi, in Puccini's opera La Boheme, is greeted with the aria 'Your tiny hand is frozen', hence somewhat cold.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to imitate them, so apes as a verb means copies.

clue.text: Go on and on about a little girl looking happy

indicators.note: going about something means surrounding it

parts.note: to rant is to talk at length and loudly
Di is a short form of the girl's name Diana

explanation.surface: Someone harangues about a small girl who seems cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: A glowing face beaming with joy shows obvious happiness.

clue.text: One looking round attic initially for ghost?

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it

parts.note: a hunter is one who looks or searches for something

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A searcher pokes around the loft, looking first for a spook.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as a made-up but logical word.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre that frequents a place is one that haunts it, so the word is a playful term for a ghost.

clue.text: Port with large lump of ice — undesirable potation ultimately

parts.note: a berg is short for iceberg

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the last letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A fortified wine served with a big chunk of ice ends up a nasty drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink of the surface; it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bergen is a major seaport on the west coast of Norway.

clue.text: Threatened — a church needing external repair

indicators.note: needing something external means requiring an outside piece, so one part wraps around the other

parts.note: to mend is to repair
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church building is in peril and requires work on its outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To be put in danger or intimidated is to be under threat, a past-tense verb matching.

clue.text: See cow run even when ill

indicators.note: something ill is out of sorts, so the letters fall into disorder

explanation.surface: A farmer notices a cow running even when it is sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cow' looks like the animal but is the verb meaning intimidate; 'See' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To cow someone is to intimidate them, sapping their courage, which matches the verb meaning to rattle.

clue.text: Lift what be light from what we hear

indicators.note: what we hear signals that a word is identified by its sound

parts.note: rays are beams, what light consists of

explanation.surface: A cryptic musing on raising things, judged by what people say about light.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is to hoist it up, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Passage men cleared before a bullfight

indicators.note: clearing something out removes it, so the men leave the passage

parts.note: a corridor is a passage
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Soldiers are cleared from a passageway before a Spanish bullfight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleared' leaves CORRID; 'men' as OR (other ranks) is a standard military abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the Spanish name for a bullfight, literally a running of the bulls.

clue.text: In Herts town notice activity in shops etc

indicators.note: one piece placed in another signals insertion

parts.note: Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire, England
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A notice posted in an English market town about business going on in its shops.
explanation.walkthrough: Herts is short for Hertfordshire, a county north of London; Tring is one of its towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying and selling goods is commerce, the business conducted in shops and markets.

clue.text: Strive on with difficulty as one looking for financial return?

indicators.note: doing something with difficulty means struggling, so the letters are strained into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who keeps striving hard in the hope of a profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who puts capital into a venture expects profit, the financial return the clue describes.

clue.text: Poor fellow with drug injection

indicators.note: an injection puts something into the body, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a man is a fellow
E is short for ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: An unfortunate chap receives a shot of drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby or inferior quality is described as poor or mean, as in a mean dwelling.
